title: Personal Information & My Local Park
sourceVersion: Life 2nd Edition A2-B1 · Unit 1 pages 17-19 · Class 19A

visualStandard.rule: Very dark blue text; large projector-first typography; colourful supporting boxes; mobile-safe layouts

interactionStandard.principle: Student Book first; PPT is reference only. Keep the printed activity number visible on every task screen.
interactionStandard.teacher: Check · Reset · Show answer · Presentation · Timer · Responses · Live Class / QR
interactionStandard.reveal: Teacher arms Show answer, then taps individual item cards. Revealed answers remain visible until Reset.

metadata.sourcePolicy: Student Book Unit 1E-1F is canonical. PPT supports visual ideas only.

screens.title: By the end of the lesson, you can…

groups.heading: KNOWLEDGE
items: recognise common information used on forms and form conventions
understand key words used in the My local park video

groups.heading: SKILLS
items: complete a form with specific information
ask and answer questions about a local park

groups.heading: OUTCOME
items: use the video questions in a short role-play

screens.title: Doctor Dash · Match the problem and advice
screens.instruction: Work with your partner. Match each medical problem with the best piece of advice. Then create one short pharmacist–patient exchange.

items.question: a bad cough
a sore throat
items.answer: drink hot water with honey and lemon

items.question: a headache
a temperature
items.answer: take your temperature and see a doctor if it continues

speakingFrame: A: I don't feel very well. I've got …
B: How do you feel? / Have you got a temperature?
B: You should … / Why don't you …?

screens.title: Forms in everyday life
screens.instruction: Look at the four form cards. Type the name of each form. Your teacher can reveal each label one by one. Then discuss the two questions from the book.
discussion: What kinds of forms do you sometimes fill in?
Think of a form you filled in. What information did you write?

screens.title: What is each form for?
screens.instruction: Read the clues and choose the correct form. Each question has three choices.

items.question: It asks for title, first name, address, current occupation, smoking and current medications.
It asks for passport number, nationality, qualifications, place of birth and marital status.

screens.title: Match the sentences with the headings
screens.instruction: Match questions 1–7 with headings A–G. Type the letter in the answer box, then Submit. Teacher: arm Show answer and tap a row to reveal the correct heading inside that row.

items.question: Are you married, single or divorced?
Do you take any pills or medicine?
How many children do you have?
What country were you born in?
What city/town were you born in?
Who can we call in your family if you need help?
What is the first letter of your middle name?

screens.title: Information on forms
screens.instruction: Type a short answer in each box. Teacher: arm Show answer and tap any card to reveal the answer in the same card.

items.question: What does DOB mean?
What does No. mean?
What do Mr, Mrs, Ms and Dr show?
Which form says PLEASE USE CAPITAL LETTERS?

screens.title: Complete the patient details
screens.instruction: The receptionist is collecting information from a new patient. Listen to the conversation and complete the three details.

items.answer: Three times a week — about three hours
Swimming sometimes; walking at weekends with friends

screens.title: Design a new-student form
screens.instruction: Choose the information your form needs. Build a simple form with your partner, then exchange it and check: Is it easy to fill in? Do you know what to write in each part? Would you change anything?

screens.title: My local park
screens.subtitle: Video · everyday life in a park

screens.title: A place to meet and relax
screens.instruction: Look at the park scene. What is this place? Then type a short answer to the two questions from the book.

questions.question: Why do people like going there?

screens.title: Match the words to the definitions
screens.instruction: Match words 1–6 with definitions A–F. Type the letter in the answer box, then Submit. Teacher: arm Show answer and tap a row to reveal the correct match.

headings.text: a region or part of a town
it has four wheels and you move babies or small children in it

what you can see around you

screens.title: Watch and number a–g
screens.instruction: Watch the video and number a–g in the order you see them. Type the letter for each position 1–7, then Submit.

choices.text: A woman is walking with her dog.
There's a large house near the park.
Two people are walking down a path.
A tractor is cutting the grass.

screens.title: Complete the notes
screens.instruction: Work in pairs. Watch again. Student A completes column 1; Student B completes column 2. Use the tabs to focus on one person at a time.

people.name: Visitor 1
people.aPrompt: When do you come to the park?
people.bPrompt: Why do you like coming to the park?
people.bAnswer: There are a lot of dogs for Jasmine to play with; beautiful trees everywhere.

people.name: Visitor 2
people.aPrompt: When do you come to the park?
people.aAnswer: Every day; after lunchtime, around 1 p.m.; on sunny days in my lunch break
people.bPrompt: Why do you like coming to the park?
people.bAnswer: It is up high and there is a beautiful view.

people.name: Visitor 3
people.aPrompt: When do you come to the park?
people.aAnswer: When we were a young family and had children, we used to come here
people.bPrompt: Why do you like coming to the park?
people.bAnswer: It has happy memories; it is nicer than the other way; it is a lovely park.

people.name: Visitor 4
people.aPrompt: When do you come to the park?
people.aAnswer: I go through the park and sometimes spend time with my friends
people.bPrompt: Why do you like coming to the park?
people.bAnswer: I like spending time in this park.

people.name: Visitor 5
people.aPrompt: When do you come to the park?
people.aAnswer: quite often / about twice a week
people.bPrompt: Why do you like coming to the park?
people.bAnswer: I like jogging and doing pull-ups; the park is quiet and has lots of flowers and trees.

people.name: Visitor 6
people.aPrompt: When do you come to the park?
people.aAnswer: I try and come to the park regularly
people.bPrompt: Why do you like coming to the park?
people.bAnswer: There are always wild flowers and blossom on the trees; it is lovely to look at.

screens.segmentNote: Segment buttons replay a short evidence window around the current visitor; timings are approximate and teacher-adjustable during Preview QA.

screens.title: Share, complete, check
screens.instruction: Share your notes with your partner and complete the other column. Then watch the video again and check all your answers.
checklist: Share only your own column first.
Watch again and correct any detail you both missed.

screens.title: Guess the person
screens.instruction: Student A chooses one person in the video but doesn't tell Student B. Student B asks the two questions from the video and guesses the person. Change roles and repeat.
questions: When do you come to the park?
model: A: I come here about twice a week.
B: Do you come here to exercise?
A: Yes. I like jogging and I like to do pull-ups here.
B: Are you the student who jogs in the park?
screens.note: The model reuses question patterns and details from the Student Book/video notes so students can substitute their chosen person's information.

screens.title: Exit check · Six quick questions
screens.instruction: Answer briefly. This is a final check, not a test.

items.question: What does DOB mean?
Which heading answers ‘What city/town were you born in?’
Name one title used before a name on a form.
What does walkway mean?
items.answer: A path or small road only for people

items.question: Which scene comes first in Activity 3?
items.answer: b · A woman is walking with her dog.

items.question: Name one question used in the park role-play.
items.answer: When do you come to the park? / How often do you come?
